full_judgment:
Syed Mahmud Hossain J: This appeal by the pre-emptors as the appellants following leave is directed against the judgment and order dated 2-7- 2003 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2387 of 1995 making the Rule absolute reversing those dated 22-10-1994 passed in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 233 of 1992 of the Court of Sub-ordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, Third Court, Chittagong allowing pre-emption case reversing those dated 30-7-1992 in pre-emption Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 1992 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Third Court, Sadar, Chittagong dismissing the pre-emption case under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act or in the alternative under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 

 7. Mr Omar Farook, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellants, submits that the High Court Division came to a finding that the pre-emptors are non co-sharers in RS Khatian No. 3838 and that on the contrary they are co-sharers in RS Khatian No. 3836 although the pre-emptors by filling an application for amendment before the appellate Court amended the application for pre- emption stating that they are also co-sharer tenants in RS Khatian No. 3838 and that the High Court Division without taking into consideration that fact delivered the judgment and, as such, the impugned judgment should be set-aside. He further submits that in case of a pre-emption under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural and Tenancy Act if a tenant is co-sharer in the plot he is also treated as a co-sharer in that plot even if the said plot is recorded in more than one khatian. 

 10. Admittedly, the pre-emptors own a portion of land in RS plot No. 3797. There is nothing on record to show that this plot was partitioned by meets and bounds between the parties and that mutation in accordance with such partition has been effected. Admittedly, the case land is situated with-in Chittagong City Corporation and, as such, section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act is attracted, not section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 

 11. In the case in hand, it appears that in the appellate Court the pre-emptors filed an application under Order VI Rule 17 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for amendment of the application for pre-emption filed under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural and Tenancy Act stating that they are also co-sharer tenants in RS Khatian No. 3838. In support of their contention, they produced a registered deed of sale dated 27-11-1940 to show that their father Md. Younus purchased land from RS Khatian No. 3838 and, as such, they are also co-sharer tenants by inheritance in that khatian. The application for' amendment was allowed by the appellate Court by Order No. 12 dated 3-6-1993. The High Court Division came to a wrong finding that the: pre-emptors are not co-sharers in RS Khatian No. 3838 and, as such, reversed the findings of the appellate Court holding that the pre-emptors are not entitled to pre-empt the case land. By amendment of the application for pre-emption, the pre-emptees could prove that they have got interest in RS Khatian No. 3838. 

 12. In a case of pre-emption filed under section 24, of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act if a co-sharer tenant owns a portion of land in any plot, he is to be. treated as co-sharer in the entire plot even if the land of that plot is recorded in more than one khatian. Therefore, in the event of transfer of a portion of land of that plot appertaining to another khatian a co-sharer tenant can file a pre-emption case under section .24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act notwithstanding the fact that he does not have any interest in that khatian. The words "one or more co- sharer tenants of such land" occurring in section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act means a co- sharer in the plot not the holding as mentioned in section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. Such being the position of law, the pre-emptors were not even required to file an application for amendment to show that they have also interest in RS Khatian No. 3838. 

 13. In the case of SM Basiruddin vs Z Islam, 35 DLR (AD) 230, it has been held that the expression 'non-agricultural land' used in section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act is not synonymous with the word 'holding' as used the "Bengal Tenancy Act or State Acquisition of Tenancy Act."
